auditFlags.description: WildApricot invoice and payment data spans April 2026 through June 2026 (and one payment in August 2025). None of these transactions fall within the QuickBooks balance sheet period of 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31. WildApricot data cannot be reconciled against the 2025-12-31 balance sheet because the activity post-dates the reporting period.
auditFlags.recommendation: Confirm the intended reporting date. If the balance sheet should reflect a 2026 period, rerun the QuickBooks report for the correct end date. If 2025-12-31 is correct, WildApricot data for 2026 is out-of-scope and should not be included.

Because these are post-period and unpaid, they do not create a liability on the 2025-12-31 balance sheet. No Unearned Membership Dues Payable or Deferred Revenue has been recorded.
auditFlags.recommendation: If the reporting period is updated to a 2026 date, these unpaid invoices should be evaluated for recognition as Accounts Receivable (if services are owed) or excluded if membership has not yet commenced.

auditFlags.description: WildApricot shows 3 paid event registrations (Diffin, Scott for 'Testing a Member Event', 'Testing Rough to Ready', and 'Test Event Invoice') with PaidSum listed as no value. Event names include 'Testing' prefixes suggesting these may be test transactions. One free registration (Arnold, Craig for 'National Craft Open Studios Weekend') requires no revenue recognition. auditFlags.recommendation: Confirm whether test event registrations should be voided or reversed in WildApricot. For production events with future service dates, evaluate deferred revenue recognition.

auditFlags.description: The QuickBooks Balance Sheet contains no Accounts Payable, Credit Cards, Unearned Skills Education Fees, Unearned Storage Fees, Membership Dues Payable, Notes Payable, Equipment, Shop Assets, Leasehold Improvements, Accumulated Depreciation, Accounts Receivable, or Prepaid Expenses. auditFlags.recommendation: Confirm with management whether these account types are applicable to the organization. If applicable, ensure all accounts are set up in QuickBooks and balances are entered prior to financial statement issuance.

scheduleO.narrative: Kansas City Woodworkers Guild Inc is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization incorporated in Missouri in 1992. The Guild's mission is to promote the art and craft of woodworking through education, community engagement, and shared access to tools and facilities. The Guild supports members at all skill levels through monthly membership meetings, educational classes (including Basic Woodworking, Intermediate Woodworking, Bandsaw Box, and Intro to Hand Tool Woodworking), special interest groups (covering hand tools, CNC, laser engraving, finishing, and carving), Rough to Ready project workshops, and community outreach events such as the National Craft Open Studios Weekend.

The Form 990 was prepared by the organization's Treasurer using QuickBooks and WildApricot financial data. The completed return was not formally reviewed by all governing body members prior to filing due to the organization's small size and limited administrative infrastructure. The Treasurer reviewed the return before signing. The organization intends to implement a formal governing body review process for future filings.

The organization makes its governing documents, conflict of interest policy (if adopted), and financial statements available to the public upon written request directed to the Treasurer at 1717 Washington St, Kansas City, MO 64108-1121. The organization does not currently post these documents on a public website.

PREPARER'S NOTE: This Form 990 was prepared using WildApricot membership management data and QuickBooks accounting data. Significant data limitations exist: (1) The QuickBooks Profit and Loss report for 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31 contains no income or expense data. All revenue figures are derived from WildApricot. (2) The majority of WildApricot invoice and payment activity (42 of 43 invoices; 37 of 38 payments totaling $6,848.00) falls in April through June 2026, outside the 2025 tax year. Only one WildApricot payment of $250.00 (dated 2025-08-05, Testing, Scott - membership application) and one donation of $10.00 (Brian Rorabaugh, undated) fall within or are attributable to the 2025 tax year. (3) The QuickBooks balance sheet equity consists entirely of Opening Balance Equity of $5,000.00, which is a QuickBooks setup artifact that should be reclassified before filing. (4) No prior-year (2024-12-31) balance sheet data was provided; beginning-of-year balances are reported as $0.00. (5) Membership dues may require proration if membership periods extend beyond December 31, 2025. CPA review and reconciliation is strongly recommended before this return is filed with the IRS.
